name: Paddock - Racing Livery Generator for Unity
summary: Designs a racing livery for every car in your roster (scheme, team colours, number roundel and fictional sponsors) and paints it onto your own vehicle meshes through their UVs.
description:
A designed racing livery for every car in your roster, painted onto your own vehicle meshes.

With Paddock, a 20-car AI grid stops being one car in 20 tints. Give it a roster (team, number, colours if you have them) and it designs the whole championship: every team gets a different scheme family, a title sponsor and minors from a generated sponsor universe, one tyre supplier and a series sponsor appear on every car, and team-mates share a livery with their own numbers. Then it projects each livery into your car mesh's own UVs and hands you an ordinary texture.

WHAT IT GENERATES

Twelve hand-authored scheme families for the flanks: Twin Stripes, Chevron, Sash, Halves, Spear, Hoops, Arrow, Fade, Checker, Wave, Dazzle and Split. Each is drawn from a seed, so every team gets its own variation, and each has a matching roof and bonnet treatment.
Twelve curated motorsport palettes, or a team's own two colours. The number's ink is chosen by WCAG contrast so it reads on its panel (at least 4.5:1 on every curated palette).
A sponsor universe per championship: names from a syllable grammar (sometimes with a trade word like OIL, TIRES or BRAKES), nine drawn marks and six decal styles. The title sponsor goes on the rear door and across the bonnet, minors on the sills and front wing, the series sponsor across every windscreen.
A roof number turned to read from the left, the right, the front, or left off.

WORDS READ CORRECTLY ON BOTH SIDES

A single mirrored side design would print numbers and sponsors backwards on one side of the car. Paddock mirrors the scheme's shapes onto the right flank and then draws the number and every sponsor again, the right way round.

PAINTED ONTO YOUR MESHES

Every triangle is rasterised in UV space and coloured from the view that faces it: left flank, right flank, top, or the nose and tail. Only the body submeshes you name are painted, so glass, tyres and trim keep their materials. Set the model's forward and up axes once. A beltline setting puts the scheme's main band and the number on the doors. If both flanks share UV space, the bake reports it in BakeReport.HasMirroredUVs instead of guessing, and it counts texels where two parts of the body overlap in UV space.

IN THE EDITOR AND AT RUN TIME

Window > CSAF > Paddock holds a roster and a garage of every car's flank, and one button bakes the roster onto the selected objects in name order, saving a texture and a material per car with Undo. The CSAF / Paddock Livery component bakes on Start from a roster entry and applies the texture through a MaterialPropertyBlock, so a material shared by twenty cars is never repainted by one of them. Livery.Compose, Sponsors.Universe and LiveryBaker.Bake touch no Unity object, so they can run on a worker thread.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Paddock/.
2. Open Demo/Scenes/PaddockDemo.unity and press Play: a 12-car starting grid painted from one generated championship. N draws a new championship, Left and Right walk the grid, Space stops the camera, R turns the roof number.
3. Open Window > CSAF > Paddock and press Create a sample roster (8 teams, 16 cars).
4. Select your car objects, set Vehicle forward, Vehicle up and Body submeshes, and press Bake roster onto N selected object(s).

Generated sponsor names are nonsense words and a list of well-known sponsor names is refused, but no generator can promise a word is nobody's trademark, so check any name you ship.
technical:
Features: a livery per car designed from a roster; 12 hand-authored scheme families with matching roof and bonnet treatments; 12 curated palettes or team colours with contrast-solved number ink; generated sponsor universe (9 drawn marks, 6 decal styles); team-mates share a livery; words redrawn the right way round on the right flank; CPU projection bake into the mesh's own UV0, body submeshes only; mirrored-UV and overlapping-UV reporting; editor window with bake-to-selection and view export; runtime component.

Number of C# scripts: 15 (13 Runtime, 1 Editor, 1 Demo). Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Paddock.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Paddock.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Paddock.Demo (demo scene).
Editor window: Window > CSAF > Paddock. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Paddock/Demo/Scenes/PaddockDemo.unity (demo car built by code).
Minimum Unity version: 2022.3. Built and tested against 6000.5.7f1.
Render pipelines: the livery is set on the material's main texture slot, found by name (_BaseMap URP, _BaseColorMap HDRP, _MainTex Built-in). Tested in the Built-in pipeline.
Meshes need UV0 with each flank on its own island, and Read/Write enabled for runtime baking.
No Resources folder, no shaders, no images, no models, no fonts, no audio, no network calls. Dependencies: none.
No third-party assets are included.

Documentation: https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/paddock/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the scheme families, the palettes, the sponsor generator, the lettering, the UV projection baker, the roster and runtime component, the editor window and the demo scene, including the demo car, which is built by code.

The liveries the package produces are not made by an image model. Every livery, letter and number is drawn by the shipped code from authored geometry. The store images are captures and composites of that output. The store cover uses an AI-generated illustration of an empty circuit as its background, with real Paddock cars rendered on top.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
